item.title: Radiative Transfer Modeling of Multi-Shell Molecular Outflows in the Class 0 Protostar IRAS 15398-3359
item.description: arXiv:2611.16805v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Recent high-angular-resolution observations of protostellar outflows have revealed complex spatial and velocity structures that are difficult to describe with a single shell. We have investigated the primary outflow of the Class 0 protostar IRAS 15398$-$3359 in the H$_2$CO and CS emission observed with ALMA and identified four shell-like components, which trace the cavity walls of the more extended CO outflows. Non-LTE radiative-transfer calculations of H$_2$CO and synthetic ALMA observations of the three-dimensional model show that a common ellipsoidal geometrical form and Hubble-law-like velocity field can broadly reproduce the channel-map and position--velocity structures of the identified shells when the geometry, spatial configuration, and kinematics of each shell are allowed to vary independently. The kinematic timescales and inclination angles of the inner and outer shells are $\sim$1000 yr ($19^\circ$ and $15^\circ$) and $\sim$750 yr ($5^\circ$ and $8^\circ$), respectively. The momentum injection rate of the outer bipolar pair is approximately 2.2 times that of the inner pair. The inferred $\dot{M}_{\rm wind}/\dot{M}_{\rm acc}$ ratios are $0.7$--$3\%$ and $2$--$7\%$ for the inner and outer shells. The observed shell-to-shell differences suggest episodicity of the mass ejection events, where the strength and direction of the outflow activity may vary over short timescales of order $10^2$--$10^3$ yr.
item.dc:creator: Yushi Ishizuka, Shigehisa Takakuwa, Kazuya Saigo, Jinshi Sai, Shu Ishibashi

item.title: A deterministic theory of kinetic fluctuations in long-range interacting homogeneous systems without collective effects
item.description: arXiv:2611.16893v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Finite-$N$ fluctuations govern the slow relaxation of long-range interacting systems, yet accessing their full statistics demands huge ensembles of costly simulations. We show that, in homogeneous systems without collective effects, this statistical problem collapses onto just three deterministic kinetic equations. Starting from the Landau-Dean-Kawasaki equation, i.e. the stochastic counterpart of the large deviation principle for the Landau equation, we derive the infinite hierarchy of $n$-point moments of the empirical distribution function at leading order in $1/N$. We prove that it is solved exactly by a quasi-Gaussian closure. The resulting minimal Landau fluctuation hierarchy is formed by the Landau equation, a Lyapunov equation for the two-point moment, and a kinetic equation for the three-point moment. From these three equations, all higher-order moments follow algebraically. The hierarchy exactly preserves the collisional invariants and their fluctuations, and predicts the full probability distribution of observables in the central fluctuation regime. Benchmarked against $N$-body realizations, it reproduces the mean, variance and higher-order moments with an accuracy that improves systematically with $N$. A single deterministic time-integration of three coupled partial differential equations thus replaces large ensembles of simulations, for any large $N$.
item.dc:creator: Anwar El Rhirhayi, Jean-Baptiste Fouvry, Julien Barr\'e

item.title: A Variable Compact Millimeter Excess in the Type-1 Seyfert Galaxy NGC 985: Implications for a Black-Hole Corona
item.description: arXiv:2611.17033v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Compact millimeter emission from radio-quiet active galactic nuclei has been proposed as a probe of magnetized accretion-disk coronae. We present three epochs of ALMA observations of the type-1 Seyfert galaxy NGC 985, together with archival post-upgrade VLA data presented here for the first time, to investigate its compact millimeter excess. The millimeter flux density decreased strongly between the first two ALMA epochs separated by approximately one month, while the component was detected again at an intermediate level in the third epoch. This variability demonstrates an intrinsically variable compact component and implies a model-independent size limit of $\lesssim 0.024$ pc ($\simeq 1.1\times10^3 R_{\rm S}$). Spectral decomposition requires a compact, self-absorbed synchrotron component to reproduce the millimeter-wave data. A hybrid thermal/nonthermal coronal model reproduces the radio-millimeter spectra, with the two broadly sampled ALMA epochs favoring different nonthermal electron distributions. The estimated radiative cooling times are comparable to or shorter than the light-crossing time, implying continuous injection or reacceleration of nonthermal electrons; a change in particle injection is the most natural driver of the observed spectral changes. We conclude that NGC 985 hosts a recurrent and variable compact millimeter synchrotron component. A magnetized corona provides a plausible origin, although the present data do not uniquely distinguish a coronal origin from alternatives such as a jet base.
item.dc:creator: Akihiro Doi, Yoshiyuki Inoue

item.title: The Synthetic Absorption Line Spectral Almanac (SALSA)
item.description: arXiv:2510.19904v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We create the first large-scale mock spectroscopic survey of gas absorption sightlines traversing the interstellar medium (ISM), circumgalactic medium (CGM), and intergalactic medium (IGM) surrounding galaxies of virtual Universes. That is, we create mock, or synthetic, absorption spectra by drawing lines-of-sight through cosmological hydrodynamical simulations, using a new mesh-free Voronoi ray-tracing algorithm. The result is the Synthetic Absorption Line Spectral Almanac (SALSA), which is publicly released on our online science platform. It spans a diverse range of ions, transitions, instruments, observational characteristics, modeling assumptions, redshifts, and numerical simulations. These include, but are not limited to: (ions) HI, OI, CI, MgI, MgII, FeII, SiII, CaII, ZnII, SiIII, SiIV, NV, CII, CIV, OVI; (instruments) SDSS-BOSS, KECK-HIRES, UVES, COS, DESI, 4MOST, WEAVE, XSHOOTER; (model choices) with/without dust depletion, noise, quasar continua, foregrounds; (redshift) from z=0 to z~6; (ancillary data) integrated equivalent widths, column densities, distances and properties of nearby galaxies; (simulations) IllustrisTNG including TNG50, TNG-Cluster, EAGLE, and SIMBA. We also provide Faraday rotation measure (RM) probing magnetic fields, and dispersion measure (DM) as traced by fast radio bursts (FRBs). The resulting dataset is generic and broadly applicable, enabling diverse science goals such as: (i) studies of the underlying physical gas structures giving rise to particular absorption signatures, (ii) galaxy-absorber and halo-absorber correlations, (iii) virtual surveys and survey strategy optimization, (iv) stacking experiments and the identification of weak absorption features, (v) assessment of data reduction methods and completeness calculations, (vi) inference of physical properties from observables, and (vii) apples-to-apples comparisons between simulations and data.
item.dc:creator: Dylan Nelson, Celine Peroux, Philipp Richter, Matthew M. Pieri, Sebastian Lopez, Rongmon Bordoloi, Siwei Zou, Joseph N. Burchett, Rebecca L. Davies, Rahul Ramesh, Matthew C. Smith, Sanchayeeta Borthakur, Christopher W. Churchill

item.title: Effect of ionizing photon escape fraction in faint galaxies on modeling reionization history of the universe
item.description: arXiv:2511.07543v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present model calculations of the reionization history of hydrogen using star formation histories, computed with a galaxy formation model which reproduces properties of local dwarf galaxies and UV luminosity functions of galaxies at $z=5-16$. We use the ionizing photon density functions predicted by the model along with different models for the escape fraction of ionizing photons, $f_{\rm esc}$, to study the effects of ionizing photons from faint galaxies and different assumptions about $f_{\rm esc}$ on the evolution of hydrogen ionized fraction with redshift, $Q_{\rm HII}(z)$. We show that accounting for the contribution of faint galaxies with UV luminosities $M_{1500}>-13$, and with a constant ionizing photon escape fraction of $f_{\rm esc}=0.1$ results in the hydrogen reionization history consistent with all current observational constraints. Comparing results of the $f_{\rm esc}=0.1$ model and two alternative models shows that the model with a strong luminosity dependence of $f_{\rm esc}$, which assigns high $f_{\rm esc}$ to faint galaxies, results in early reionization inconsistent with observational constraints. However, the model in which $f_{\rm esc}$ follows a universal redshift-independent correlation with the recent maximum specific star formation rate, motivated by the results of the SPHINX galaxy formation simulation, results in the reionization history in good agreement with existing observational constraints, even though this model produces a sizeable ionized hydrogen fraction of $Q_{\rm HII}\approx 0.15-0.2$ at redshifts $z=8-12$. Our results show that the relative contribution of faint dwarf galaxies to reionization depends sensitively on assumptions about the escape fraction for galaxies of different luminosities, and that this is the main source of uncertainty in modeling hydrogen reionization.
item.dc:creator: Zewei Wu, Andrey Kravtsov, Harley Katz

item.title: NGDEEP: A New Nonparametric Measure of Local Star Formation and Attenuation at Cosmic Noon
item.description: arXiv:2512.11989v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce a new non-parametric technique to quantify the spatially-resolved relationship between the local star formation rate (SFR) and dust attenuation. We apply it to 12 star-forming galaxies at 1.0<z<2.4 using JWST/NIRISS slitless spectroscopy from the NGDEEP survey. First, we construct spatially resolved (~1 kpc per pixel) Balmer decrement ($\Ha/\Hb$) maps of these galaxies and derive their corresponding dust attenuation and intrinsic SFR maps. We rank-order the map pixels by attenuation and construct a cumulative distribution curve of the total SFR as a function of increasing attenuation. We define $\mathrm{A(\Ha)}^{\mathrm{SFR}}_{10\%}$, $\mathrm{A(\Ha)}^{\mathrm{SFR}}_{50\%}$, and $\mathrm{A(\Ha)}^{\mathrm{SFR}}_{90\%}$ as the dust attenuation levels behind which 10%, 50%, and 90% of the total integrated SFR is screened, respectively. These metrics quantify the probability that a given star-forming region lies behind a given level of attenuation. Across the sample, 50% of the local star formation occurs behind an attenuation of 2.9 mag or higher ($\mathrm{A(\Ha)}^{\mathrm{SFR}}_{50\%}$) on average. This indicates that the bulk of star formation in these galaxies is significantly attenuated by dust. The value of $\mathrm{A(\Ha)}^{\mathrm{SFR}}_{10\%}$ equals 0.6 mag for the average profile, indicating that even the least attenuated star-forming regions are still highly attenuated. The globally measured attenuation more closely matches $\mathrm{A(\Ha)}^{\mathrm{SFR}}_{10\%}$ than $\mathrm{A(\Ha)}^{\mathrm{SFR}}_{50\%}$. This suggests that the global value is weighted toward the least dust-obscured star-forming regions and significantly underestimates the typical attenuation a star-forming region encounters. Our results demonstrate a new approach for understanding the extremely dusty local conditions of the star-forming interstellar medium in star-forming galaxies at cosmic noon.
item.dc:creator: Grace M. Forrey, Raymond C. Simons, Jonathan R. Trump, Lu Shen, Anton M. Koekemoer, Micaela B. Bagley, Steven L. Finkelstein, Casey Papovich, Nor Pirzkal

item.title: Group Pre-processing in J1611+4026: Minor Rejuvenation of a Massive ETG fueled by Interaction-driven Gas Transfer
item.description: arXiv:2602.22904v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Interactions within galaxy groups are fundamental drivers of galactic evolution, and establishing a direct observational link between the dynamical processes of satellite galaxies and the rejuvenation of massive host galaxies remains challenging. We present a multi-wavelength work of J1611+4026, a unique triple system characterised by a massive early-type host galaxy, Component C and two gas-rich companions, Components A and B, which are currently undergoing a major merger in its near environment. Utilising deep optical imaging from DESI-LS and spectroscopic data from DESI and P200, we employ 2D morphological decomposition using \textsc{GALIGHT} alongside joint spectrophotometric synthesis modelling with \textsc{BAGPIPES} and \textsc{CIGALE} to deconstruct the structural properties and star formation histories of the member galaxies. Crucially, we identify an asymmetric tidal tail extending $\sim$15.15 kpc from Component A, confirming the ongoing interaction between the companions. Although Component C appears quiescent in both morphology and spectroscopy, we reveal a subtle robust signal of ``minor rejuvenation'', characterised by significant internal dust extinction of $E(B-V) \sim 0.53$ and a UV excess. The reconstructed star formation history indicates a recent ($\sim$100 Myr) starburst that contributes a negligible fraction to the total stellar mass ($f_{\rm burst} < 0.1$ per cent). We propose that this activity is fueled by the accretion of metal-enriched gas stripped from the interacting companions. These results strongly suggest group pre-processing, where interactions between satellite galaxies drive low-level star formation in the massive host through gas transfer, providing a quantitative benchmark for interaction-driven evolution in dense environments.
item.dc:creator: Yaosong Yu, Qihang Chen, Zizhao He, Limeng Deng, Liang Jing, Jianhui Lian

item.title: Apparent Stability in Self-Gravitating Turbulence and the Evolution of Molecular Clouds
item.description: arXiv:2604.10699v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Recent observations of hydrostatic structure and virial equilibrium in supersonically turbulent, self-gravitating molecular clouds imply a stability that contrasts with the transcience of turbulent structure. To investigate this contradiction, we model a molecular cloud as a turbulent eddy and study its evolution as a dynamical system. In a two-dimensional phase space of structure and energy, we find that the dynamical equilibrium is a saddle point, stable in the direction aligned with force balance, but unstable in the direction of energy balance because of the combination of the turbulent dissipation and the negative heat capacity of self-gravitation. Near the saddle point, evolutionary trajectories follow a characteristic pattern that first approaches the equilibrium before departing in the direction of instability. Since the phase-space speed is proportional to the virial and energy imbalance, trajectories slow near the equilibrium resulting in a local overdensity of clouds. Also, near equilibrium, the relaxation to force balance is faster than the growth rate of the instability in energy. Consequently, more clouds are observed in near equilibrium states with hydrostatic structure even though the equilibrium is metastable. This resolves the apparent contradiction of equilibrium structure observed in dynamically unstable, self-gravitating turbulence.
item.dc:creator: Eric Keto

item.title: Suppression of star formation at the centre of barred AGN galaxies
item.description: arXiv:2605.23269v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We measured the Concentration (C) index of H\alpha and CO (J = 2-1) in 17 nearby star-forming galaxies from the PHANGS survey. We have found four barred spiral galaxies with a C(H\alpha)/C(CO) ratio of ~ 0.3-0.4, while the other 13 galaxies exhibit ratios of ~ 1 (range from 0.7 to 1.3). All four barred galaxies with low ratios host active galactic nuclei (AGNs), consistent with a scenario in which star formation is suppressed by mechanical and radiative feedback from the AGN. Therefore, negative feedback is effective in these four barred galaxies with a low molecular gas mass fraction (< 0.1), even when AGN activity is relatively weak. The formation of bar structures causes molecular gas to collect in the central region, leading to starburst activity. However, after the starburst, the remaining gas becomes inefficient for star formation rapidly due to AGN feedback. It can mean the quenching process occurs more rapidly in AGN-barred galaxies. Furthermore, since gas remains in the central region, AGN activity is likely to continue. These quenching processes are a unique mechanism found in barred spiral galaxies and are essential to understanding galaxy evolution.
item.dc:creator: Takashi Yamamoto, Nario Kuno, Daisuke Iono, Takuya Hashimoto, Sophia K. Stuber, Daizhong Liu, Thomas G. Williams, Akio K. Inoue

item.title: The Doppler effect of the Milky Way rotation on mHz gravitational waves
item.description: arXiv:2606.11115v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We model the stellar density and the rotation curve of the Milky Way and compute the gravitational-wave spectrum of its unresolved binaries as a function of direction. Because the Galaxy rotates, the waves emitted along each line of sight are Doppler-shifted by a different amount, and we derive for the first time the resulting observed anisotropic spectrum, which no longer factorizes into a spectral shape times an angular template. We then quantify the observability of this distortion with space-based interferometers. With their nominal noise budgets, neither LISA nor a LISA+Taiji network can detect it: the residual between the models that include and neglect the rotation has a signal-to-noise ratio ${\rm SNR}_{\rm diff}\simeq0.2$ and $0.7$ after two years, and the induced bias on the foreground parameters stays below $0.1\sigma$. A tenfold better noise amplitude, of the order contemplated for post-LISA concepts, raises the residual to ${\rm SNR}_{\rm diff}\simeq4.6$ for the network, where the effect becomes measurable and displaces the spectral cutoff by half of the statistical error.
item.dc:creator: Giorgio Mentasti, Quentin Baghi

item.title: The Incidence of Large Ionized Bubbles at Redshift 13
item.description: arXiv:2606.17571v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Ionized bubbles around the first galaxies connect early galaxy growth, ionizing photon escape, intergalactic-medium topology, Ly$\alpha$ visibility, 21~cm structure, and reionization timing. We model the incidence of galaxy-driven ionized bubbles at $z\approx 13$ using JWST UV luminosity functions, taking the Ly$\alpha$ source reported by Witstok et al. as a benchmark for the relevant scale. We quantify regions with comoving radius $R\ge 2.5$~cMpc through their sky surface density $\Sigma_{\ge 2.5}$. For our continuously active fiducial case, using the Donnan et al. UVLF with $f_{\mathrm{esc}}=0.2$, $\log\xi_{\mathrm{ion}}=25.5$, $f_{\mathrm{active}}=1$, and $C=3$, we find $\Sigma_{\ge 2.5}\simeq 8.10\times 10^{-3}$ arcmin$^{-2}$ per $\Delta z=1$. For $f_{\rm active}=0.2$ or $f_{\rm time}=0.2$ with 10~Myr mean on-times, the incidence falls by factors of 4.1 and 2.9, respectively; longer correlated episodes strengthen the tail. Merging overlapping spheres raises the fiducial incidence by $9.5\%$. The simulations show that Witstok-sized regions can arise in UVLF-calibrated galaxy-driven models. This is a population-level statement, and the specific Witstok source may still require unusual effective ionizing efficiency, recent fading or burstiness, or a non-stellar ionizing contribution.
item.dc:creator: Peter Ziwei Hu, Massimo Stiavelli, Colin Norman

item.title: First measurement of narrow-line flux ratios for a lensed quasar with JWST/NIRSpec IFS
item.description: arXiv:2606.23808v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Strong gravitational lensing is a powerful probe of dark matter (DM) structure on subgalactic scales: in particular, statistics of flux-ratio anomalies (discrepancies between mass model predictions and observed flux ratios) in quadruply imaged quasars are sensitive to perturbations by low-mass DM halos down to $\sim 10^6 M_\odot$. Studies leveraging these anomalies require high-quality flux-ratio measurements from an emission region insensitive to stellar microlensing. In this paper, we present the first measurement of narrow-line flux ratios for a gravitationally lensed quasar using JWST/NIRSpec with Integral Field Spectroscopy (IFS), targeting the well-studied system RXJ1131$-$1231. Flux ratios are extracted from the [S III] 9071/9533 $\r{A}$ narrow-line doublet - the first use of this doublet for substructure studies - by performing a full lens model reconstruction to isolate the unresolved nuclear emission from extended narrow-line emission. The resulting spectra are jointly modeled using $\texttt{lensqso-specfit}$, a publicly available software package introduced in this work for the simultaneous spectral fitting of multiple lensed quasar images. We achieve $\sim$ 5% uncertainties on the flux ratios, comparable to the precision of JWST/MIRI warm dust measurements, and detect a clear anomaly in the cusp images relative to a standard smooth lens model. Our results are in good agreement with previous narrow-line measurements and broadly consistent with JWST/MIRI warm dust flux ratios, with marginal ($\sim 2-3\sigma$) deviations. We illustrate how such shifts between differently sized emission regions may be enhanced by small ($\sim 10$ pc) spatial offsets. Our method is generalizable to other systems with existing or future IFS observations, and the combination of narrow-line and warm dust flux ratios offers a new avenue for improving DM constraints with flux-ratio anomaly statistics.
item.dc:creator: Hadrien Paugnat, Tommaso Treu, Anna M. Nierenberg, Anowar J. Shajib, Shawn Knabel, Daniel Gilman

item.title: Uncertainty-Aware Deep Learning for the Ly$\alpha$ Forest: CNN-Based Absorber Detection and Characterization
item.description: arXiv:2607.05494v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Ly$\alpha$ forest is a powerful probe of the intergalactic medium and small-scale matter distribution, but deriving absorber properties traditionally requires computationally expensive Voigt-profile fitting. We present a convolutional neural network (CNN) that identifies and characterizes H I Ly$\alpha$ absorbers directly from quasar spectra. The model is trained on synthetic spectra generated from the IllustrisTNG simulation and fitted with the VIPER Voigt-profile fitting code to provide training labels. The network simultaneously predicts absorber presence, column density ($N_{\rm HI}$), Doppler parameter ($b_{\rm HI}$), and line centroid. On simulated spectra, the CNN reproduces the viper reference catalogue with an F1 score of $\sim$0.8, with mean absolute errors of $\sim$0.18 in $\log N_{\rm HI}$ and $\sim$0.10 in $\log b_{\rm HI}$. It reproduces the H I column density distribution function and the $b_{\rm HI}$--$N_{\rm HI}$ relation obtained from viper, recovering similar CDDF slopes and a lower-envelope relation with an RMS difference of only 0.36 km s$^{-1}$. Applied to UVES spectra, performance decreases to an F1 score of $\sim$0.5, with mean absolute errors of $\sim$0.35 in $\log N_{\rm HI}$ and $\sim$0.22 in $\log b_{\rm HI}$. Latent-space analysis reveals a significant domain shift between the simulated and UVES spectra, contributing to the reduced performance. Nevertheless, the CNN reproduces the observed CDDF and $b_{\rm HI}$--$N_{\rm HI}$ distributions obtained from the viper catalogue, yielding CDDF slopes consistent with VIPER and a lower-envelope RMS difference of 3.20 km s$^{-1}$ relative to viper. Monte Carlo dropout is implemented during inference to quantify predictive uncertainties. Together with its computational efficiency, the method provides a scalable and uncertainty-aware framework for Ly$\alpha$ forest analysis in upcoming spectroscopic surveys.
item.dc:creator: Paryag Sharma, Vikram Khaire, Ting-Yun Cheng, Hum Chand, Prakash Gaikwad

item.title: The Road to Normalcy: Environment-Driven Evolutionary Pathways for Primordial Black Holes
item.description: arXiv:2608.23498v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate how cosmological environment regulates the evolution of primordial black hole (PBH) seeds in the early universe using a suite of hydrodynamical simulations. PBHs, formed during the radiation dominated epoch, offer a possible source of early BH seeds that does not require prior star formation. We find that PBHs follow distinct evolutionary pathways depending on the gas supply and halo assembly history. In underdense regions, limited inflow suppresses both accretion and star formation, producing faint, metal-poor systems, while in overdense environments, sustained gas inflow drives rapid BH growth and the formation of compact, centrally concentrated stellar components. These differences lead to large variations in BH-to-stellar mass ratio, metallicity, and morphology, collectively bracketing a range of possible evolutionary pathways for PBH-seeded systems. Some pathways pass through a phase with compact stellar structure and elevated BH-to-stellar mass ratio that resembles observed Little Red Dots, before evolving into more extended galaxy--AGN systems. Our results suggest that both the initial seed properties and cosmological environment jointly shape early BH--galaxy co-evolution, while subsequent environmental regulation can erase the memory of the initial seeding channel.
item.dc:creator: Saiyang Zhang, Junehyoung Jeon, Boyuan Liu, Volker Bromm, Priyamvada Natarajan

item.title: Revisiting the enigmatic sixth star cluster in the Fornax dwarf spheroidal galaxy
item.description: arXiv:2608.27270v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Fornax dwarf spheroidal (dSph) galaxy is one of only two Local Group dSphs that host a population of globular star clusters (GCs), the present-day properties of which have often been used to investigate the nature of the dark matter. An additional overdensity of stars called Fornax 6, lying at a projected distance of $\sim$0.3 kpc from the galaxy centre, was recently identified as a sixth GC residing in Fornax. However, this conclusion was based on relatively shallow photometric observations and a limited number of spectra. Here, we reinvestigate the nature of Fornax 6 by analysing MUSE/Wide-Field-Mode observations alongside deep GMOS-S imagery. Using a sample of 131 spectra of red giant and red clump stars, we confirm the Fornax 6 overdensity as a distinct chemo-dynamical component with respect to the surrounding field population. Specifically, we identify 43 likely members associated with the cluster, from which we measure $\rm [Fe/H]=-0.63\pm0.03\,$dex, $\overline{v_{los}} = 50.8^{+0.8}_{-0.7}\, \rm km\,s^{-1}$, and $\sigma_v = 3.3^{+1.4}_{-1.9}\, \rm km\,s^{-1}$. The main-sequence turn-off, observed here for the first time, strongly suggests that these stars are coeval and well described by a $\sim$3 Gyr old isochrone. The cluster is characterised by an irregular morphology, a large half-light radius ($R_h=8.8^{+1.1}_{-1.3}\,$pc), a small flattening ($e<0.26$, 68\% upper limit), and low luminosity ($M_V = -5.0 \pm 0.4$). Our improved characterisation of Fornax 6 supports its classification as a genuine low-mass cluster likely undergoing tidal disruption, making it the youngest and most metal-rich member of Fornax's unique GC system.
item.dc:creator: Chiara Crociati, Annette M. N. Ferguson, Raffaele Pascale, Sebastian Kamann, Silvia Martocchia, Jess M. Howell, Pete B. Kuzma, Dougal Mackey, Sakurako Okamoto, Masato Onodera

item.title: JWST/NIRSpec Reveals Diverse Nuclear Environments in Dwarf Galaxies Hosting AGN
item.description: arXiv:2609.04315v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Dwarf galaxies, in the $\Lambda$CDM framework, are expected to dominate the galaxy number density at all redshifts. As such, studying AGN in these systems, including characterizing their local environments and emission properties, is essential in obtaining a comprehensive view of the AGN population and their influence on their host galaxy. To this end, we present JWST/NIRSpec IFU observations of four dwarf galaxies (M$_\star<$10$^{9.5}\;$M$_\odot$) with evidence of AGN activity. Utilizing the improvements in resolution and sensitivity offered by JWST, we investigate the emission features of the central kiloparsec of these dwarfs. Our findings include the detection of over 100 emission lines across our sample, including coronal lines with ionization potentials greater than 300 eV. The nuclear spectra show diverse emission features. In two galaxies, we measure strong contributions from hot dust to the infrared continuum. We also detect both PAH and coronal line emission within 100 parsecs of the nuclei in three galaxies. We estimate the hot H$_2$ gas mass to be between 1--20 M$_\odot$ within 300 pc across our sample, where both thermal and non-thermal excitation are involved. Lastly, spatial flux maps reveal varied emission structures across all observed gas phases, ranging from radial symmetry around the nucleus to elongated plumes. Kinematic maps also show each galaxy has unique velocity structures despite all being isolated, affirming the diversity of rotation curves problem, a long standing tension between simulations and observations. These results showcase the unique and varied nuclear environments that can be found in dwarf galaxies hosting AGN.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Bohn, Archana Aravindan, Gabriela Canalizo, Aditya Togi, Shobita Satyapal, Tohru Nagao, Matthew Malkan, Thomas S. Y. Lai, Hanae Inami, Weizhe Liu, Marina Bianchin, Tanio Diaz-Santos, Aaron Evans, Sean T. Linden, Vivian U, Lee Armus, Loreto Barcos-Munoz, Kirsten Larson, Yiqing Song, Sabrina Stierwalt, Jason Surace

item.title: A Self-Consistent Jeans Analysis of the Milky Way Rotation Curve
item.description: arXiv:2609.30364v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Jeans-based measurements of the Milky Way (MW) rotation curve (RC) have revealed a declining outer RC. The interpretation, however, depends sensitively on the tracer selection, the tracer density profile, gradient terms in the Jeans equation, and non-axisymmetric perturbations in the outer disk. We present a more self-consistent Jeans analysis of the MW RC and reassess whether the outer decline remains after a revised treatment of the main Jeans terms and their associated systematic uncertainties, including those related to non-axisymmetric perturbations. We select a kinematically homogeneous disk tracer sample designed to retain stars on nearly circular disk orbits, removing only 12\% of the original sample. We estimate the tracer density profile from the same stars used for the kinematic moments, rather than adopting an external scale length. We find that the tracer density profile is better described by a double exponential over the validated range 12.5 < R < 21 kpc. We also assess the main systematic uncertainties associated with the fiducial Jeans equation terms, including the often neglected cross term, and account for different rotational velocities in the outer disk substructures. The derived RC remains nearly flat in the inner disk and declines at large radii. Over the adopted outer interval, $R\gtrsim16\,\mathrm{kpc}$, the RC slope is consistent with a Keplerian decline even after accounting for the systematic uncertainties. The corresponding mass modeling gives an extrapolated dynamical mass of $2.01^{+0.10}_{-0.08}\times10^{11}\,M_\odot$.
item.dc:creator: Yongjun Jiao (Department of Astronomy, Tsinghua University, Beijing 100084, China), Francois Hammer (LIRA, Observatoire de Paris, Universite PSL, CNRS, Meudon 92195, France), Istiak Akib (LIRA, Observatoire de Paris, Universite PSL, CNRS, Meudon 92195, France), Yanbin Yang (LIRA, Observatoire de Paris, Universite PSL, CNRS, Meudon 92195, France), Haifeng Wang (Local Universe and Time-Domain Astronomy Laboratory, Department of Astronomy, China West Normal University, Nanchong 637002, China)

item.title: Mergers may not be the main channel for galaxy stellar mass growth at redshift $z\gtrsim5$: Predictions from cosmological hierarchical models and simulations
item.description: arXiv:2610.17575v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Mergers are a crucial channel of galaxy growth, but their role relative to star formation remains uncertain at high redshift. Here we investigate merger rates and merger-driven stellar mass assembly for galaxies with stellar mass $M_\star \gtrsim 10^8 \, {\rm M_{\odot}}$ at $z\simeq 5-11$, by combining complementary theoretical approaches within $\Lambda$CDM. These include the DECODE semi-empirical model, the TNG100 and EAGLE hydrodynamical simulations, and the \textsc{L-Galaxies} semi-analytical model, together with the Millennium and TNG100-Dark simulations used to examine dark matter subhalo statistics and merger timescales. This compares models with different treatments of baryonic physics and galaxy-halo connections. We find that dark matter-only simulations predict merger timescales $\sim 30\%$ longer than those inferred from cosmological simulations including baryons. Galaxy major merger ($M_{\rm \star,sat} / M_{\rm \star,cen} > 0.25$) rates show a substantial model- and mass-dependent redshift evolution. Despite high rates, mergers contribute only $\lesssim 10\%$ to the total cosmic stellar mass density evolution. The average ex-situ stellar mass fraction ranges from a few percent to $\sim 25\%$ for all stellar mass bins at $z\gtrsim 5$, across different models and simulations. Their broad agreement implies that stellar mass assembly at cosmic dawn is dominated by in-situ star formation rather than mergers. These findings suggest that the high pair fractions identified by JWST may not directly trace efficient ex-situ stellar mass growth, highlighting the need for physically motivated merger timescales to interpret galaxy assembly in the early Universe.
item.dc:creator: Hao Fu, Mohammadreza Ayromlou, Francesco Shankar, Andrea Lapi, Daniel Roberts, Feng Yuan, Maulik Bhatt, Evgenii Chaikin, Simona Gallerani, Luca Graziani, Antonio La Marca, George Mountrichas, Yingjie Peng, Haocheng Wang, Kai Wang

item.title: Euclid Quick Data Release (Q1). XLV. Data processing for intracluster light measurements
item.description: arXiv:2610.29682v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Euclid survey provides images with extraordinary potential for studies of the low-surface-brightness Universe, including intracluster light (ICL). However, to realise this promise, the data must be carefully treated to minimise background variations while preserving the signal from diffuse structures. In this work, we describe the post-processing and measurement procedures used for studies of ICL with Euclid. We demonstrate a substantial reduction in background variations without resorting to a small-scale background subtraction. By injecting simulated clusters into the real images, we show that our approach preserves the faint outskirts of extended sources. On scales of several arcminutes, we can reliably detect surface-brightness levels around 27.5 mag arcsec$^{-2}$ in $Y_\textrm{E}$, $J_\textrm{E}$, $H_\textrm{E}$, and 29 mag arcsec$^{-2}$ in $I_\textrm{E}$. As a result, we can obtain accurate measurements of the ICL in individual clusters from the local Universe out to z~0.8 with uncertainties of the order of 10% in surface brightness, 10 degrees in position angle, and 0.1 in ellipticity. Our ability to measure the diffuse light with Euclid is thus set to meet expectations and revolutionise our understanding of the ICL.

item.title: Euclid Quick Data Release (Q1). XLVII. The shape of cluster haloes revealed by intracluster light
item.description: arXiv:2610.29683v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Intracluster light (ICL) offers a luminous route for measuring the shapes and orientations of cluster haloes. We used Euclid Quick Data Release (Q1) images to quantify ICL shapes for 205 clusters at $0.1 \leq z \leq 0.8$ selected from the eROSITA All-Sky Survey and the Dark Energy Survey. We measured the ICL properties across five bands ($I_\mathrm{E}$, $Y_\mathrm{E}$, $J_\mathrm{E}$, $H_\mathrm{E}$ and the coadded $YJH_\mathrm{E}$), and find that the shape parameters are consistent across the filters, with the $H_\mathrm{E}$ band probing the profiles to the largest cluster-centric distances ($0.1R_{200\mathrm{c}}\sim100$ kpc). The ICL ellipticity ($e=1-b/a$) distribution peaks at 0.5, consistent with halo ellipticities inferred from strong and weak lensing studies, suggesting that the ICL traces the large-scale structure of the clusters. Cluster cores, dominated by brightest cluster galaxy (BCG) light, are round ($e\sim0.2$), while the ICL becomes progressively more elongated at large radii, reaching an ellipticity of $\sim0.5$ by $0.1R_{200\mathrm{c}}$. We find that the ICL is closely aligned with the BCG (87% lie within 30$^\circ$), but shows a weaker alignment with the satellite galaxy distribution (61% within 30$^\circ$). Robust position angles could be measured using the ICL for 63% of the sample, whereas position angles could be measured for only 30% of the sample using the satellite galaxies. Stacking clusters in redshift bins allows measurements of the ICL surface brightness to $0.6$-$0.8R_{200\mathrm{c}}$ and ellipticity beyond $0.3$-$0.4R_{200\mathrm{c}}$ (300-400 kpc), but we observed a plateau in the ICL ellipticity beyond $0.1R_{200\mathrm{c}}$. These results demonstrate the capability of Euclid to characterise the ICL morphology with high statistical precision, allowing new constraints on cluster halo structure and its evolution with redshift.

item.title: Euclid Quick Data Release (Q1). XLVIII. A systematic study of the intracluster light fraction at 0.2 < z < 1.5
item.description: arXiv:2610.29684v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present a homogeneous analysis of the intracluster light (ICL) in approximately 300 galaxy clusters spanning $0.2<z<1.5$, combining Sunyaev-Zeldovich-selected clusters from the South Pole Telescope and optically selected clusters from Euclid, and comparing results with Hydrangea simulations. We measured the brightest cluster galaxy (BCG) within elliptical isophotes of semi-major axis 50 kpc, and ICL between 50 and 200 kpc. We show that the Euclid Wide Survey can detect ICL in individual massive clusters ($M_{500} \gtrsim 10^{14.2}\,M_{\odot}$) out to at least $z\sim1.5$, with detection rates of 70-80%. This indicates that diffuse stellar envelopes are common, although not ubiquitous, in massive clusters throughout this redshift range. Using a uniform methodology, we place improved constraints on ICL fraction evolution. ICL contributes about 40% of the combined BCG and ICL light and 20% of the total cluster stellar light, with both fractions remaining approximately constant across $0.2<z<1.5$ at fixed cluster mass. This implies that the relative partitioning of stellar mass between the BCG, ICL, and satellite populations is largely established by $z\sim1.5$. However, the ICL properties of individual clusters may still change as they evolve, since the sample does not represent an evolutionary sequence. This behaviour is consistent with a scenario in which the BCG and ICL are assembled together through the accretion, stripping, and eventual merging of the same population of massive galaxies ($>10^{10}\,M_\odot$). The inferred ICL fraction also depends systematically on wavelength, while remaining largely insensitive to the adopted outer integration radius of 200-600 kpc. These results highlight the importance of homogeneous ICL analyses and constrain the evolution of diffuse stellar components in clusters.

item.title: Euclid Quick Data Release (Q1). XLVI. The metallicity of the intracluster light
item.description: arXiv:2610.29686v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Colour provides key information to constrain the stellar population of the intracluster light (ICL), the diffuse light within galaxy clusters. We derive radial colour profiles ($Y_\mathrm{E}-H_\mathrm{E}$, $J_\mathrm{E}-H_\mathrm{E}$, $I_\mathrm{E}-H_\mathrm{E}$) of the brightest central galaxy (BCG) and ICL for 168 galaxy clusters from the Dark Energy Survey redMaPPer catalogue within the redshift range $0.1 < z < 0.75$ and halo mass $M_{\rm 200m} > 10^{14.05}M_\odot/h$, within the Euclid Quick Data Release (Q1). By stacking the light profiles measured using elliptical annuli on the BCG and ICL images, we reliably measure the ICL colour out to approximately 300 kpc, over which we find a colour gradient, with the ICL becoming bluer than the BCG out to approximately 150 kpc. Using stellar population synthesis (SPS) models, we find that near-infrared (NIR) colours are sensitive to metallicity, but not age. Thus, we measure a metallicity profile in the BCG and ICL that extends out to 300 kpc for a statistical sample for the first time. While the colours, and the detection of a colour and metallicity gradient, are robust, we note that our metallicity measurement is dependent upon our choice of both SPS model and colour. We find that the metallicity of the BCG is super-solar [$\log_{10} (Z/Z_\odot) > 0.1$], while the ICL is metal-poor [$\log_{10}(Z/Z_\odot)\approx -0.5$], placing the first statistical constraint on the metallicity of the ICL out to large radii. These results support our current understanding of BCG and ICL formation: BCGs form predominantly through mergers with massive galaxies or the cores of satellite galaxies, while the ICL grows via the tidal stripping of lower-metallicity stars from the outskirts of massive satellite galaxies.

item.title: Can the $\sim 5$ kpc starburst ring in the Milky Way create the eROSITA bubbles?
item.description: arXiv:2610.40049v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: eROSITA bubbles (eRBs) in our Galaxy are thought to be due to the energy injection by the central star-forming region or the central supermassive black hole. Identifying the origin of these bubbles is crucial in constraining the origin of the Fermi Bubbles and the nature of the Galactic feedback. However, some recent opinions suggest that the eRBs may not even have been produced by any central source, but rather a result of a star-formation ring at $R\sim 5$ kpc. In this letter, we perform detailed hydrodynamic simulations to refute that claim and show that such a ring of star formation alone is not able to produce the symmetric eROSITA bubbles - one needs a compact energy injection from the Galactic Center to produce these bubbles. Our study, therefore, suggests that the eROSITA bubbles truly represent the nuclear outflow from our Galaxy.
item.dc:creator: Mukesh Singh Bisht, Kartick C. Sarkar

item.title: FORGE'd in the Early Universe II: Constraining the Pop III Initial Mass Function
item.description: arXiv:2611.08598v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present a cosmological radiation-magnetohydrodynamics (RMHD) zoom-in simulation of $56$ Population III stars using FORGE'd in FIRE. Our simulation combines a cosmological initial condition centered on an isolated ultra-faint galaxy ($M_{\mathrm{halo}} \sim 10^9 M_\odot$ at $z=0$) with individual-star formation and feedback physics, reaching a maximum mass resolution of $\sim 10^{-2} M_\odot$ and spatial resolution of $\sim 10^{-3} \mathrm{pc}$. We follow continued star formation for just over $500$ Myr, from $z \sim 16$ to $z \sim 7$, substantially longer than what has been achieved before, and track star formation across five distinct minihalos. From our stellar population, we self-consistently resolve an emergent stellar initial mass function (IMF) and find $\alpha = 1.9$ for $dN/dM \propto M^{-\alpha}$ at $M_{\star} \gtrsim 2.2 M_{\odot}$. Additionally, we form both single and multiple stellar systems, including binaries and higher-order multiples, as well as stars with masses below $1 M_{\odot}$. At early times, the stellar mass distribution is more top-heavy, with a high-mass slope of $\alpha\sim1.4-1.5$, similar to previous Pop. III simulations, and steepens as star formation continues. This suggests that differences between our final IMF and previous studies may partly reflect the much longer evolution followed here, approximately five orders of magnitude longer than in several previous Pop. III sink-particle simulations. The first star-forming minihalo, which hosts the most massive stars in our simulation, has a shallower IMF slope of $\alpha\approx 1$, while later-forming minihalos produce lower maximum stellar masses in lower-density parent clouds.
item.dc:creator: Yasmine J. Meziani, Philip F. Hopkins, Pratik J. Gandhi, Claude-Andr\'e Faucher-Gigu\`ere, Michael Y. Grudi\'c, Shivan Khullar, Vasilii Pustovoit

item.title: r-Process Abundance Variations in Globular Clusters as Fossils of Turbulent Mixing
item.description: arXiv:2611.14472v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Several metal-poor Galactic globular clusters exhibit substantial star-to-star $r$-process abundance variations at nearly fixed [Fe/H], with the ensemble suggesting smaller variations toward increasing metallicity. We investigate whether this chemical structure can be inherited from incomplete mixing in the galactic environments in which the clusters formed. Using parsec-scale simulations of rare-element transport in a supernova-driven turbulent disk, we follow the redistribution of $r$-process ejecta and characterize the abundance structure of gas selected to trace star-forming environments. Rare enrichment events generate strong [Eu/Fe] inhomogeneities that persist across a range of physical scales. As chemical evolution proceeds, the available abundance variance decreases, while spatial averaging over larger regions reduces the differences between their characteristic abundances. The simulations provide substantial pre-collapse $r$-process variance at low [Fe/H] and show the same broad decline toward higher metallicity suggested by the globular-cluster measurements. Our results support an interpretation in which at least some of the observed $r$-process variations are inherited from pre-existing chemical structure in the natal environment, allowing globular clusters to preserve a fossil record of the mixing history between rare enrichment and star formation.
item.dc:creator: Lailani Kenoly, Isabelle Connor, Melinda Soares-Furtado, Evan N. Kirby, Nia Imara, Enrico Ramirez-Ruiz

item.title: Gravitational Waves from Collisions of Fuzzy Dark Matter Solitons
item.description: arXiv:2412.19262v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: According to the Schr\"odinger-Poisson (SP) equations, fuzzy dark matter (FDM) can form a stable equilibrium configuration, the so-called FDM soliton. The SP system can also determine the evolution of FDM solitons, such as head-on collision. In this paper, we first propose a new adimensional unit of length, time and mass. And then, we simulate the adimensional SP system with $\mathtt{PyUltraLight}$ to study the GWs from collision of FDM solitons when the linearized theory is valid and the GW back reaction on the evolution of FDM solitons is ignored. Finally, we find that the GWs from collisions have a frequency of (few ten-years)$^{-1}$ or (few years)$^{-1}$ when FDM mass is $m=10^{-18}\rm{eV}/c^2$ or $m=10^{-17}\rm{eV}/c^2$. Therefore, future detection of such GWs will constrain the property of FDM particle and solitons.
item.dc:creator: Chen Tan, Jing-Kang Bin, Ke Wang

item.title: Flare genesis in relativistic jet: Disentangling the drivers of variability in the blazar 4C +27.50
item.description: arXiv:2504.18927v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Recently, blazar 4C +27.50 was found to be flaring in gamma-rays since its detection with Fermi-LAT in 2008. For the first time, a dedicated temporal and spectral study of the blazar 4C +27.50 has been performed in this work to understand the nature of this object. We used the Bayesian block algorithm to identify four flaring states and one quiet state in the 4-year-long Fermi-LAT light curve. Simultaneous broadband flaring episodes have been observed, and a significant correlation is seen between optical and $\gamma$-ray emission, suggesting the co-spatial origin of the broadband emission. The variation of fractional variability amplitude with respect to frequency shows a nearly double hump structure similar to broadband SED. The fastest flux doubling time in the 1-day binned $\gamma$-ray light curve is found to be about 7.8 hours. A curvature in $\gamma$-ray spectra has been observed, possibly caused by a stochastic particle acceleration process rather than radiative cooling. No evident correlation was found in the $\gamma$-ray flux-index plot, but a clear harder-when-brighter trend is observed in the X-ray flux-index plot. A one-zone leptonic model has been implemented to understand broadband emission during the quiet and flaring states, and the variation of the jet parameters has been investigated. Broadband SED modeling suggested that an enhancement in the magnetic field and particle energy density, together with a harder particle spectrum, might have caused the flaring events, while the bulk Lorentz factor shows no systematic change.
item.dc:creator: Joysankar Majumdar, Sakshi Maurya, Raj Prince

item.title: Robust Amortized Simulation-Based Inference via Learned Error Models
item.description: arXiv:2509.05724v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Recent advances in neural density estimation have enabled amortized Bayesian inference for complex stochastic simulators. However, these methods rely on simulators accurately reflecting the true data-generating process and can degrade significantly under model misspecification. We consider the setting where multiple unlabeled observations are available and introduce robust variational neural posterior estimation (RVNP), an amortized Bayesian inference method that uses an importance-weighted autoencoder to jointly learn a misspecification-robust posterior proxy and an explicit error model that captures the simulation-to-reality gap. Our results show that RVNP can recover robust posterior inference in a data-driven and interpretable manner, outperforming previous methods on multiple metrics across misspecified benchmarks.
item.dc:creator: Matthew O'Callaghan, Kaisey S. Mandel, Gerry Gilmore

item.title: Spatial Profiles of 3I/ATLAS CN and Ni Outgassing from Keck/KCWI Integral Field Spectroscopy
item.description: arXiv:2510.11779v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Cometary activity from interstellar objects provides a unique window into the environs of other stellar systems. We report blue-sensitive integral field unit spectroscopy of the interstellar object 3I/ATLAS from the Keck-II-mounted Keck Cosmic Web Imager on August 24, 2025 UT. We confirm previously reported CN and Ni outgassing, and present, for the first time, the radial profiles of Ni and CN emission in 3I/ATLAS. We find a characteristic $e$-folding radius of $593.7\pm14.8$ km for Ni and $841.0\pm15.4$ km for CN; this suggests that the Ni emission is more centrally concentrated in the nucleus of the comet and favors hypotheses involving easily dissociated species such as metal carbonyls or metal-polycyclic-aromatic-hydrocarbon molecules. Additional integral field spectroscopy after perihelion will offer a continued opportunity to determine the evolution of the radial distributions of species in interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS.
item.dc:creator: W. B. Hoogendam, B. J. Shappee, J. J. Wray, B. Yang, K. J. Meech, C. Ashall, D. D. Desai, K. Hart, J. T. Hinkle, A. Hoffman, E. M. Hu, D. O. Jones, K. Medler, C. Pfeffer

item.title: QPEs from Warped Disk Collisions with EMRIs: Brightness-Recurrence Diagram and Gravitational-Wave Follow-up
item.description: arXiv:2605.24905v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Quasi-Periodic Eruptions (QPEs) display correlated long/short and strong/weak patterns that remain unexplained by existing flat-disk collision models. We propose that these features arise from an extreme-mass-ratio inspiral (EMRI) colliding with a warped accretion disk, likely formed after a tidal disruption event. The warp modulates both recurrence time and burst energy, encoding the disk geometry -- and thus the spin of the central supermassive black hole (SMBH) -- into the X-ray light curve. We introduce the Brightness-Recurrence Diagram (BRD) to visualize this correlation, where QPE bursts trace an elliptical trajectory driven by the EMRI's apsidal precession; the tilt of this ellipse encodes whether the EMRI is prograde or retrograde relative to the SMBH spin. Applying this model to the prototypical QPE source GSN 069 successfully reproduces the observed patterns. The data are consistent with either a prograde stellar secondary or a retrograde stellar-mass black hole. In the stellar-mass black hole scenario, ongoing orbital decay could render the EMRI detectable by LISA within a few decades, facilitating gravitational-wave follow-up and independent multimessenger constraints on the system.
item.dc:creator: Bo-An Chen, Bei You, Giovanni Miniutti, Ning Jiang, Zhen Pan, Tao Yang, Xi-Long Fan, Kai Liao, Xu-Heng Ding, Zong-Hong Zhu, Shuai-Kang Yang, Sai-En Xu, Han He, Xiao Fan

item.title: Cooling, conduction, and compact objects: Gravothermal evolution of dissipative self-interacting dark matter halos
item.description: arXiv:2606.19428v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Many proposed self-interacting dark matter (SIDM) models yield radiative processes that can dissipate energy. Understanding their impact on astrophysical objects through simulations and comparing the results with observations may thus constrain SIDM models. We systematically investigated how dissipation alters the gravothermal evolution of isolated SIDM halos by independently varying dissipation and heat conduction and identified potential observational signatures. We present the first extension of the $N$-body formalism for frequent small-angle self-interactions to include effective dissipation. We compared all results for isolated halos with a dissipative gravothermal fluid model to assess the validity and limitations of the latter. We find that dissipation qualitatively changes the gravothermal evolution of SIDM halos beyond simply accelerating collapse. Sufficiently strong central cooling can invert the usual role of heat conduction: the formation of an isothermal core is suppressed such that conduction remains directed inward throughout the evolution. Outer halo regions beyond the scale radius can cool efficiently rather than being heated by conduction, resulting in a larger region of mass infall and a less pronounced indentation between the core and the outer halo in the final density profile. These effects depend strongly on the cooling rate but are comparatively insensitive to the angular dependence of the self-interaction cross section. We further show that weakly dissipative self-interactions can explain the properties of the recently observed strong lens perturber in JVAS B1938+666 with significantly shorter evolution times or, equivalently, smaller cross sections compared to the elastic case. Our results open a new route to connecting halo structure and recently reported compact objects to dark-sector microphysics.
item.dc:creator: Ludwig D. Schmidt, Moritz S. Fischer, Mathias Garny

item.title: Dynamical flattening of halo density cusps by Q-ball dark matter
item.description: arXiv:2607.28517v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Cold, collisionless dark matter successfully explains a wide range of observations, including the formation of large-scale structure. Nevertheless, tensions remain on small, galactic scales, most notably the cusp-core, or inner-mass-deficit, problem and the diversity of inner rotation-curve shapes and central densities at fixed halo mass. These observations suggest that additional dark-sector physics may affect the inner structure of halos, although no generally accepted explanation has yet emerged. Here, making use of a toy but representative model, we investigate how interacting dark-matter Q-balls -- non-topological solitons stabilized by a conserved charge -- modify halo centers and generate a diversity of inner profiles. Our calculations include merger-induced mass and kinetic-energy losses, elastic heat transport, and the gravitational readjustment of the halo; flattening and later recontraction can both occur. Produced in the early Universe in the dark sector, these Q-balls grow in the dense central regions of halos, while their interaction cross section decreases as the soliton mass increases. This process operates preferentially in halo centers, converting part of the rest-mass energy stored in massive Q-balls into relativistic dark-sector particles and thereby modifying the inner mass-density profile. The resulting density-dependent energy loss competes with heat transport and halo response. An ensemble of initial assembly conditions yields very different final densities at fixed microphysics, although neither a universal constant-density core nor a statistical fit to the observed population is established.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Libanov, Sergey Troitsky

item.title: Late-Time Evolution of the Massive Stellar Merger M101 OT2015-1
item.description: arXiv:2609.12981v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Luminous red novae (LRNe) are astronomical transients arising from unstable mass transfer and common envelope phases in close binary systems, eventually culminating in stellar mergers. Their cold, expanding ejecta provide the ideal conditions for molecule and dust formation. We investigate the late-time dust and molecular evolution of the LRN M101 OT2015-1, a high-mass LRN progenitor ($18\pm 1$M$_\odot$), using multi-band near-infrared (NIR) and mid-infrared (MIR) observations spanning up to ~5 years post-outburst. Archival and unpublished photometry from NEOWISE, Spitzer, Keck NIRC2 and MOSFIRE, are interpolated via 2D Gaussian process regression. Spectral energy distributions (SEDs) are modelled with 1D spherical radiative transfer models to track the evolution of dust mass, dust temperature, and central source properties. At +150d post-peak, the SED is well-fit by a pure stellar blackbody ($T_{\rm eff}=3330$K) with negligible dust (log$M_{\rm dust}/$M$_\odot<-6.36$). Rapid dust condensation begins around day +200 ($T_{\rm dust}=1591$K), with dust mass increasing to log$M_{\rm dust}/$M$_\odot =-3.65$ and optical depth reaching $\tau_V =64$ by +1300d. A prominent NIR re-brightening at ~600d ($M_K=-12.04$), accompanied by a dust reheating bump ($T_{\rm dust}=1567$K), highlights a second phase of dust nucleation likely driven by shock interactions. Low-resolution NIR MOSFIRE spectra are analysed for line identification and also using an LTE isothermal slab model to characterise CO molecular features. The MOSFIRE spectra reveal an O-rich environment with photospheric expansion velocities of ~$520-620$km s$^{-1}$, as measured in the Pa$\beta$ emission line, and high CO column densities (log$N_{\rm CO}$/cm$^{-2}=20.9$ and $20.7$ at +142d and +197d, respectively). These results confirm that LRNe are prolific producers of cosmic dust and are efficient molecular factories.
item.dc:creator: Marco A. G\'omez-Mu\~noz, Nadejda Blagorodnova, Tomasz Kami\'nski, Gerard Garcia-Moreno, Maxime Wavasseur, Hugo Tranin, Grace Katusiime, Jacob E. Jencson, Mansi M. Kasliwal

item.title: Discovery of the Slowest Radio Pulsar in the Small Magellanic Cloud
item.description: arXiv:2610.12143v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We report the discovery of a new radio pulsar PSR J0103$-$72 in the Small Magellanic Cloud (SMC) through a reanalysis of Parkes/Murriyang archival observations targeting supernova remnants and pulsar-wind nebulae in the SMC. Previously two pulsars were discovered in these observations, and PSR J0103$-$72 is the third which we independently detected in two observations of its target field. It has a spin period of 1.327 sec and a dispersion measure (DM) of $272\pm13~\mathrm{pc\,cm^{-3}}$, making it the slowest known radio pulsar in the SMC with the second-highest DM. We did not identify any plausible supernova remnant or pulsar-wind nebula associated with the pulsar. Subtracting the predicted Galactic foreground leaves a DM contribution of $\sim 230$--$242~\mathrm{pc\,cm^{-3}}$, which may suggest a long path through the ionized medium of the SMC, enhanced ionized gas along the sightline, or both. Although these data had previously been searched using both FFT and fast folding algorithms, our FFT-based reprocessing found PSR J0103$-$72 through search techniques which have previously been highly effective in discovering a large number of pulsars in other surveys. This discovery shows that candidates with weak Fourier-domain significance can reveal faint, narrow-duty cycle pulsars missed in earlier extragalactic pulsar searches.
item.dc:creator: Weiyu Wang, Rahul Sengar

item.title: A Parsec-scale Circumstellar Shell Around VX Sgr: Mass Loss and RSG/T\.ZO Nature
item.description: arXiv:2610.20689v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A thin, arc-shaped shell is discovered surrounding VX Sagittarii (VX Sgr), the largest known CSM shell around an RSG at a scale $r\sim0.59\,\mathrm{pc}$. The nebula has an extinction-corrected H$\alpha$ intensity $I_{\mathrm{H}\alpha}\sim38\,\mathrm{R}$ and an ionized mass $\sim0.1\,\mathrm{M_\odot}$. The slow $12\,\mathrm{km\,s}^{-1}$ peculiar velocity of VX Sgr and the lack of far-infrared emission in the arc indicate that it is not produced by a bow shock, but is likely instead steady RSG wind or ejecta that is photoionized by a nearby $\mathrm{O}$- or $\mathrm{B}$- type star. The nature of VX Sgr is debated in the literature as a red supergiant/hypergiant (RSG/RHG), super-AGB star, or Thorne--\.Zytkow Object (T\.ZO). Using the kinematic age of the Sgr OB1 association, the super-AGB model is disfavored. A spectroscopic test of the arc is proposed to potentially distinguish an RSG from a possible T\.ZO. The mass-loss rate is estimated from the geometry and emission measure of the shell, finding $\dot{M}\approx4\times10^{-5}\,\mathrm{M}_\odot\,\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$. The future interaction of the supernova (SN) ejecta of VX Sgr and the surrounding circumstellar material (CSM) is briefly explored through the mass ratio $\Lambda$ of the shell and SN ejecta; the interaction would likely not have a significant effect on the SN forward shock.
item.dc:creator: Julian Shapiro
